meaningEn: to rise, arise, get up, mount up, ascend, attack

collocations: French sourge-, stem of sourdre “to rise, swell,” from Latin surgere “to
rise, arise, get up, mount up, ascend; attack,” contraction of surrigere, from

assimilated form of sub- (up from below) + regere (to keep straight, guide).
Meaning “high, rolling swell of water” is from 1520s; figurative sense of
and roll forcefully” is from 1560s. Related: Surged; surging.
